citation.authors: Cai X, Canaday F, Gao S, Merrell E et al

cited_by.title: Lung function tests and race correction in spirometry

record.population: 6,107 spirometry tests in a 2010 to 2020 retrospective cohort, self-identified Black and White patients
record.design: Retrospective cohort comparing race-specific and GLI-Global interpretation with one-year outcomes
record.finding: Switching to the race-neutral approach reclassified 530 results (9%) for FEV1 and 595 (10%) for FVC. Black patients reclassified as abnormal had higher healthcare use and worse outcomes, including hospitalisation, than those consistently normal; White patients reclassified as normal also had worse outcomes, including higher mortality. The authors say clinical judgment is needed for results near the cut-off.
record.note: Single health system, US; the abstract text was cut off before the final limits sentence.
